newsitem.title: USA: OTS files charges against U.S. thrift ex-president.
newsitem.headline: OTS files charges against U.S. thrift ex-president.

text.p: The U.S. Office of Thrift Supervision said Monday it filed charges against the former president of Eureka Homestead Society for alleged unauthorized securities trading.
The alleged activity cost the New Orleans thrift $8.2 million, OTS said. The regulator of thrifts said it was seeking restitution and to ban Paul Clayton from banking.

Clayton's attorney, Patrick Fanning, said his client's position was "that he acted with authority and that the board ratified everything." Clayton is no longer in banking and the amount of damages sought is beyond his means, Fanning said.
Clayton worked at Eureka from 1980 to October 1993, when he resigned at the request of Eureka's directors, OTS said.
OTS charged that starting in 1987 until his resignation, Clayton allegedly engaged in unauthorized investment transactions on behalf of Eureka that resulted in the loss.
OTS accused Clayton of repeatedly executing documentation which falsely represented that he was authorized to open margin accounts and trade on margin on behalf of the thrift.

Clayton was also accused of not recording the alleged unauthorized trading and losses, so Eureka's financial reports were "false and inaccurate during the entire time of Clayton's trading activities," OTS said.

Eureka Homestead has since regained its former health, OTS said. Clayton has 20 days to respond to the charges, OTS said. An administrative law hearing will take place in the New Orleans area at a date to be determined, OTS said.
